  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  September 27, 2022

TO:  HEAR Commission

BY:  Aldo Cervantes, Community Development Director

SUBJECT:  Discussion regarding a Street Name Change Guidelines

  SUMMARY

On May 3, 2022, the City Council directed staff to draft guidelines for street name changes. To
help facilitate the drafting of such guidelines, the City Council directed staff to solicit feedback
and comments from the HEAR Commission, Planning Commission and the Historic
Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission. The attached guidelines have been drafted
by City staff and reviewed by the City Attorney, Public Works, Police, and Fire Department.
Comments from these Departments have been incorporated into the draft.

BACKGROUND

To assist with the origins of this matter, staff has provided the Commission with the following
background and details. In 2013, Hing Wa Lee submitted a request to the City Council to
consider a street name change for the street currently known as W. Bencamp Street to Hing
Wa Lee Place. The street segment known as W. Bencamp Street is located between Del Mar
Avenue and the Alhambra Wash Flood Control Channel just south of Valley Boulevard. The
requested segment of W. Bencamp Street is approximately 240 feet long, and located east of
San Gabriel Square. The applicant’s business, Hing Wa Lee Jewelers (1635 S. Del Mar Avenue),
is located adjacent to the south side of W. Bencamp Street. The remainder of W. Bencamp
Street on the west side of San Gabriel Square would remain unchanged.

At the August 20, 2013 City Council meeting, staff requested not only the approval of
Ordinance 603-C.S. for the street name change, but also a general policy for administering
such a program. At this meeting, Ordinance 603-C.S. was unanimously approved on the first
reading.

On September 3, 2013, the item was presented to Council to consider approving Ordinance
603-C.S. on the second reading. After a discussion regarding the matter and receiving public
   Street Name Change Guidelines
  September 27, 2022
  Page 2

input, the City Council voted to defer the action and direct staff to provide further input. At
this meeting, the Council expressed the following:

1.  Concerns regarding the Hawaii Supermarket parking requirements, which may affect
  whether or not the parcel at the southeast corner of Del Mar and Bencamp can be
  developed. If the parcel at the southeast corner of Del Mar and Bencamp is needed
  for Hawaii Supermarket parking, then that may diminish the possibility of
  development on that property;
2.  To provide additional outreach to the neighboring community inviting input; and
3.  To establish a formal policy for street name changes.

With respect to item number 3 above, staff advised the Council that a formal policy was not
necessary given how infrequent requests such as these were received. In fact, prior to this
request, the last known street name change occurred on February 3, 1998. The item was
continued to the October 15, 2013 City Council meeting. At this meeting, 13 residents spoke
in opposition to the request while 11 spoke in support. Subsequent to public comments and
Council deliberation, a motion was made to deny the request and maintain the street as W.
Bencamp Street. Such a motion was made despite a request to create a policy. The motion
to deny the request for the street name change passed on a 3 to 2 vote of the Council.

At the May 3, 2022 City Council meeting, the Council discussed this matter as well as the
re-submitted request to change W. Bencamp Street to Hing Wa Lee Place. As a result of this
discussion, the Council directed staff to draft guidelines rather than a policy to help manage
these types of requests. Prior to implementing such guidelines, the Council directed staff to
seek feedback from the HEARS Commission, Planning Commission, and the Historic
Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission.

Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission

At the September 14, 2022 Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission (HPCRC)
meeting, the Commission expressed overall support for the guidelines and suggested a few
amendments and considerations. The following includes the comments and feedback
provided:

  1) Although a majority of the Commission felt the fee was adequate, a few of the
  Commissioners felt the fee should be in line with the processing fee for a Mills Act
  application. The Mills Act application is currently set at $2,315 with a $5,000 deposit.
   Street Name Change Guidelines
  September 27, 2022
  Page 3

  2) The Commission expressed concerns regarding the use of “civic identity,” which is
  referenced under section 4.1 of the draft guidelines. The Commission would rather
  see “civic identify” either defined or replaced.
  3) The Commission expressed interest in a hierarchy system for the selection of names
  for streets, such as having geographic location as the first tier.
  4) Include and define a “Legacy Business” and include it in the selection process for a
  street name.

ANALYSIS

Roll of the Commission

The purpose of this campaign is to discuss these guidelines with the listed groups and seek
the advice and feedback from subject-matter experts. Each Commission provides its very
own unique views regarding this topic and the goal of each Commission is to provide
changes, feedback, or comments on this matter as they may relate to experiences on the
respective Commissions. The proposed changes and feedback provided in the process will
be shared with the Council at a future meeting.

There are two areas of these guidelines that may not be amended, which are authority and
the adoption process. The authority for approving or denying street name change requests
rests with the City Council. In order to formally approve a street name change, the street
name change must be adopted via legislative action and the approval of an Ordinance.

Authority

As stated above, the City does not have a formal policy or guidelines for facilitating street
name change requests. The City’s Municipal Code is also silent on this matter. According to
City of San Gabriel Code Section 100.137, Duty of the Community Development Director to
Assign Numbers, the Director shall have the duty to assign to the owner, agent or occupant
of any building the proper number thereof, determined in accordance with the provisions of
this subchapter, upon an application made. For Council’s reference, the subchapter deals
with the assignment of addresses for buildings within the City.

It’s important to note that such requests are so infrequent, that a policy or guidelines
regarding the matter would largely go unused or may encourage more requests. Staff
recommends that the City deal with such requests on a case-by-case basis and present them
to the City Council for consideration as they arise. If a request were to arise, staff would
prepare an ordinance for consideration for the City Council.
   Street Name Change Guidelines
  September 27, 2022
  Page 4

Filing Fee

Subsequent to staff’s research on this item, staff recommends a filing fee in the amount of
$726. In addition, staff proposes a deposit of $1,000 to cover for material expenditures such
as costs of notification to businesses and/or residents that domicile on a street subject to the
application. In response to the HPCRC request to increase the fees, its important to note that
fees are intended to be equitable and reflect the cost for services. The fee listed above reflects
what it would cost the City for labor and materials for processing a street name change.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission discuss the matter and provide comments to
staff regarding the draft guidelines, the application, and the proposed fee.

STREET NAME CHANGE GUIDELINES – EXISTING STREETS

1. PURPOSE

  1.1 To provide guidelines for street renaming requests, that promotes the City’s
  positive image and identity through the use of street names that are indicative of
  San Gabriel’s unique historical, geographic and cultural characteristics, and that
  assists in accurately locating properties. The quick and efficient delivery of
  emergency services, goods and services and mail, is also a key objective.

2. SCOPE

  2.1 These guidelines apply to the requests for the renaming of existing streets,
  avenues, boulevards, etc. within the City of San Gabriel.

3. RESPONSIBILITY

  3.1 The Community Development Department, Planning Division is responsible for
  the coordination and assignment of new street names within the City of San Gabriel
  and providing City Council with recommendations regarding the renaming of
  existing streets.

  3.2 City Council approval and adoption by Ordinance is required for changing the
  name of any existing street within the City of San Gabriel.

  3.3 The City will give Public Notice of a request or intention to change the name of
  any existing street within the City of San Gabriel.

4. GUIDELINES AND SELECTION OF NAMES

  4.1 The City of San Gabriel strives to ensure that all street names promote San
  Gabriel’s civic identity. Street names shall be indicative of the distinctive social,
  historical, geographic or cultural characteristics and qualities of San Gabriel.

  Selection of Names

  4.2 That street names shall be chosen, wherever possible, to recognize the historical
  significance of figures, groups, neighborhoods, places, landmarks and events
  within the City of San Gabriel that denote:

  a) The community’s evolution and progress;

  b) The unique aspects related to the community’s geographical location or
  other distinct characteristics;

  1
   Street Name Change Guidelines - 2022

  c) Figures, events, milestones, and achievements the community may wish
  to acknowledge; or

  d) Other categories not covered in a) through c) above that have been
  endorsed by resolution of City Council.

  4.3 A street name should not be given in recognition of any living person.

  4.4 That there shall be no use of awkward, corrupt, discriminatory or derogatory
  names in regard to race, sex, color, creed, political affiliation, or other social factors.

  4.5 That the Street Naming Policies, Guidelines and Procedures shall apply to public
  roadways. Private roadways, such as condominium roadways, where names are
  deemed to be in the interest of public safety shall also be applied to these
  guidelines.

  4.6 Proposed Street name must not be identical or similar sounding to any existing
  street name (both within the City and surrounding municipalities).

  4.7 Street Names, wherever practical, shall be only one-word names and shall not
  exceed 16 characters including spaces. The length shall not include the designator;
  e.g. “Street,” “Drive,” “Road.”

  4.8 Street extensions should continue with existing street names.

  4.9 Substantiation is required for proposed street names, (Historical/Personal
  significance) if there is any. (i.e. person’s last name).

5. STREET NAME TYPE DESIGNATIONS

  Wherever possible the following street name type designations are to be followed:

  5.1 Streets running in an East/West direction are to be designated as Streets.

  5.2 Streets running in a North/South direction are to be designated as Avenues,
  Roads or Drives.

  5.3 The same suffix name is generally retained for straight roads and streets upon
  the same alignment.

  5.4 Narrow secondary streets having less than a 50-foot right-of-way, are to be
  designated as Lanes.

  5.5 Wider collector streets, when separated by a planted median, may be
  designated as Boulevards or Drives.

  2
   Street Name Change Guidelines - 2022

  5.6 Dead-end streets less than 1000 feet in length are to be designated as Ways.

  5.7 Streets having two entrances in the form of a loop or an “L‟, are to be
  designated as Circle or Way.

  5.8 Any other designations are to be approved by Community Development
  Department in consultation with Fire, Police and Public Works Departments.

6. APPLICATION PROCESS

  6.1 All street name changes require the submission of an “Application for Street
  Name Change”, to the Community Development Department, Planning Division,
  for acceptance of the submitted replacement street names and subsequent
  approval and adoption by the City Council.

  6.2 The Application must include a proposed replacement street name and
  location, a sketch of the street and extent/segment of the road to be re-named, a
  petition with the name, address and signatures of 50% of the assessed property
  owners/residents who reside or own property which fronts onto or is abutting the
  subject street, and a non-refundable processing fee payable to the City of San
  Gabriel.

  6.3 The City of San Gabriel reserves the right to rename any street, including
  duplicate street names, in the interest of public safety.

  6.4 The City of San Gabriel shall not be responsible or liable for any costs associated
  with a street name change. The applicant for the street name change shall include
  the associated fees and the required deposit.

7. STREET NAME SIGNS

  7.1 Street name signs shall be of such size, shape, color and font and constructed
  of such materials as required by the Public Works Department, in compliance with
  City standards and The Manual of Uniform Traffic Control Devices. The Public
  Works Department will procure and install new or replacement signs determined
  as needed and prepare an invoice to reflect the actual costs.

8. NOTIFICATION

  8.1 The City shall notify all internal departments, the post office, agencies/bodies
  and adjacent municipalities of the change of an existing street name.

  8.2 The applicant shall be responsible for notifying other non-governmental
  organizations.

to change the name of any existing street for all Applications for Street Name

  STAFF REPORT
Date:  August 20, 2013
To:  Steven A. Preston, FAICP, City Manager
From:  Jennifer Davis, Community Development Director
By:  Algis J. Marciuska, PE, Senior Civil Engineer
  Daren Grilley, PE, City Engineer
Subject:  Ordinance No. 603-C.S. Changing the Name of Bencamp
  Street, from Del Mar Avenue to the Alhambra Wash, to Hing
  Wa Lee Place

  SUMMARY

Hing Wa Lee Jewelers is currently building an 11,000 square foot jewelry center at
1635 South Del Mar Avenue. The project has frontage on both Del Mar Avenue and
on Bencamp Street. The owner has filed a request to change the name of Bencamp
Street between Del Mar Avenue and the Alhambra Wash to Hing Wa Lee Place. Staff
recommends that City Council approve the requested name change.

I.  BACKGROUND

Hing Wa Lee Jewelers (Hing Wa Lee) located at 1635 South Del Mar Avenue is currently
constructing its new flagship store in San Gabriel. Hing Wa Lee is one of the top sales tax
producers in San Gabriel, and identifying the local street serving the project can serve to
better market and publicize Hing Wa Lee which is beneficial to economic development. The
project site has public street frontage along Del Mar Avenue and along Bencamp Street.
Hing Wa Lee has requested a street name change for the short segment of Bencamp Street
from Del Mar Avenue west to the Alhambra Wash Flood Control Channel. Following the
procedure established for an address change, Hing Wa Lee filed an application, letter of
request, and the $1,180 fee. Bencamp Street is a short segment of street, 225 feet in length,
with a parking lot and the Hing Wa Lee property on the south side and a parking lot and
commercial building on the north side. The commercial building has an address on Del Mar
Avenue. Currently, there are no buildings or businesses that have an address on this segment
of Bencamp Street.
   Street Name Change Request: Bencamp Street to Hing Wa Lee Place
  August 20, 2013
  Page 2 of 2

II.  ANALYSIS

The Police, Fire and Public Works Departments have reviewed and accepted this request.
Staff does not believe that Bencamp has historical significance. It is believed to be the
combination of the last names of two businessmen--Mr. Benjamin and Mr. Campbell--who
developed properties in the area. Approval of this change would reflect the changes in our
dynamic and diverse community. This street would be the first Chinese street name in the
city. The use of Place is common for short streets and courts, such as this street segment.

If Council approves this request, the property address would change from 1635 South Del
Mar Avenue to the recommended 118 West Hing Wa Lee Place. Police, Fire, Public Works,
the US Postal Service, County Assessor, utility companies serving the area, adjoining
property owners, and mapping organizations would be notified of the name change so they
may update their records accordingly. Hing Wa Lee would be charged for the cost of
overhead street name signs to hang on the new traffic signal mast arms and for post-
mounted street name signs at the intersection.

There are two other segments of Bencamp Street in the city. One is located between New
Avenue and Abbot Avenue, and the other is located west of Palm Avenue. They would not
be affected by this street name change.

Approval of this change by Council would establish a general policy for street name changes.
Staff believes that it is appropriate to allow renaming of short segments of minor
commercial or residential streets which would serve some historical, economic, or social
purpose. In contrast, it would generally not be appropriate to rename arterials, collectors or
long segments of streets that have many homes or businesses on them.

III.  RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council approve Ordinance No. 603-C.S. changing the name
of Bencamp Street, from Del Mar Avenue to the Alhambra Wash, to Hing Wa Lee Place.

Date:  October 15, 2013
To:  Steven A. Preston, FAICP, City Manager
From:  Jennifer Davis, Community Development Director
By:  Algis J. Marciuska, PE, Senior Civil Engineer
  Daren Grilley, PE, City Engineer
Subject:  Second Reading of Ordinance No. 603-C.S. Changing the
  Name of Bencamp Street, from Del Mar Avenue to the
  Alhambra Wash, to Hing Wa Lee Place

  SUMMARY

Hing Wa Lee Jewelers is currently building an 11,000 square foot jewelry center at
1635 South Del Mar Avenue. The project has frontage on both Del Mar Avenue and
on Bencamp Street. The owner has filed a request to change the name of Bencamp
Street between Del Mar Avenue and the Alhambra Wash to Hing Wa Lee Place.
Council approved Ordinance No. 603-C.S. at its August 20th, 2013 meeting. During
its September 3rd, 2013 meeting, Council voted to defer action on the second reading
of the ordinance and directed staff to provide further input.

I.  ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Council requested that staff provide additional information and bring this item back to
Council for further input. Issues of concern raised at the August 20th meeting included:

  1. The Hawaii Supermarket parking requirements which may affect whether or not
  the parcel at the southeast corner of Del Mar and Bencamp can be developed. If
  the parcel at the southeast corner of Del Mar and Bencamp is needed for Hawaii
  Supermarket parking, then that may diminish the possibility of development on
  that property.
  2. Providing additional outreach to the neighboring community inviting input.
  3. Establishing a formal policy for street name changes.
   Street Name Change Request: Bencamp Street to Hing Wa Lee Place
  October 15, 2013
  Page 2 of 3

A letter dated the 3rd of September 2013 from Mr. Paul Yen who owns property on
Bencamp was submitted at the August 20th meeting, and the letter indicated that Mr. Yen
opposes this street name change. A proposed development site plan was attached to Mr.
Yen’s letter. The plan appears to show new development on the north and south sides of
Bencamp Street. Additionally, several members of the public indicated that they were
opposed to the street name change as well for such reasons as the change may be construed
as favoritism toward a particular business and that Hing Wa Lee was not a historical figure in
San Gabriel.

Response to Issue No. 1

Regarding parking for Hawaii Supermarket and the need for additional parking on the
property that it leases, Planning staff researched a Community Development Department
staff report on a proposal to demolish two homes on single family parcels (which adjoin the
Hawaii Supermarket property) on Bencamp Street east of Del Mar and replace them with
parking areas. The report was from December 2007, and it stated, “As proposed, the project
will satisfy the City’s parking requirements, offering all required parking on-site. There are
currently 125 existing parking spaces. The code requires 180 parking spaces. The applicant
is providing an additional 43 spaces on Bencamp, restriping the existing parking lot and
adding an additional 14 spaces, therefore providing a total of 182 parking spaces. This
would take the site from a deficit of 55 parking spaces to a surplus of two parking spaces.”
The proposal was not approved, and it appears that the 55 spaces are still needed. This
indicates that the parking lot that Hawaii leases on the property next to Hing Wa Lee is
needed for parking.

Response to Issue No. 2

In order to allow for more input, on the 27th of September 2013, letters were sent to
adjoining property owners and residents within the boundaries of Valley Blvd. on the north,
Palm Avenue on the east, Dewey Avenue and Norwood Place on the south, and Abbot
Avenue on the west. The owners and residents on Bencamp between Jackson and Abbot
and on Bencamp east of Del Mar also received letters. Residents were requested to provide
input to the Community Development Department by the 10th of October 2013, and a
summary of input received will be provided at the Council Meeting on the 15th of October.

Response to Issue No. 3

Street name changes in San Gabriel are relatively rare. After the year of incorporation of our
City, only a handful of street name changes have been made. Once the process of
incorporation was complete and many initial changes were made to street names to make
them more appropriate to the City, the changes became very rare. The last street name
change involved changing Junipero Serra Drive to Mission Road (from the westerly city
boundary to the Union Pacific Railroad) and Mission Drive (from the UPRR to the easterly
city boundary) to Mission Road. As Council noted at its previous meeting, this particular

bencamp street\st name change bencamp st 10152013 rev 02 oct.docx
   Street Name Change Request: Bencamp Street to Hing Wa Lee Place
  October 15, 2013
  Page 3 of 3

change is unique. Because of this, staff does not recommend establishing a formal policy for
changing street names.

The legality of street names and changing them, public street naming lies solely within
jurisdiction of City Council. Bencamp is a public street, and its right of way is owned solely
by the City. It is not an easement or a private street. Staff is providing this information to
Council to assist with making the decision on this matter. Again, staff does not believe that
Bencamp has historical significance. It is believed to be the combination of the last names of
two businessmen--Mr. Benjamin and Mr. Campbell--who developed properties in the area.
Approval of this change would reflect the changes in our dynamic and diverse community.
This street would be the first Chinese street name in the city.

II.  RECOMMENDATION

Staff initially recommended that City Council approve this ordinance based on support of
economic development in the City. Ultimately, it is at the Council’s discretion to approve
any street name change. Staff recommends that Council consider the additional information
submitted when deciding whether or not to approve Ordinance No. 603-C.S. changing the
name of Bencamp Street, from Del Mar Avenue to the Alhambra Wash, to Hing Wa Lee
Place.
